links.comparator_used: Risk groups alone (categorized or dichotomized predicted risk, without ranking by continuous probability) under resource constraints
links.outcome: Positive predictive value, sensitivity and mean rank of true positives when prioritizing patients under resource constraints (simulation, plus real data from a Singaporean emergency department)
links.effect: No numeric values in the abstract. Ranking by continuous predicted risk outperformed risk groups alone. The benefit grew with model discrimination and outcome prevalence, was robust to poor calibration, and was greatest when resource constraints were highest.
links.quote: Using predicted probabilities to rank patients by predicted risk led to model performance benefits when compared to risk groups alone.

design_hint: retaining continuous risk scores for ranking instead of risk groups
